  "reasoning": "The spec describes a combinational half adder named TopModule with one-bit ports a, b, sum, cout. A half adder has exactly two independently checkable output behaviours -- the sum bit and the carry-out bit -- so the decomposition is two requirements, one reference-model method each. The interface paragraph and the port list are not behaviour on their own, so per the instructions they are attributed to the requirements they constrain: the preamble sentence (module name, and all ports one bit) plus the a/b/sum port lines are claimed by the sum requirement starting at offset 0, and the cout port line by the carry-out requirement. The half-adder sentence is claimed by both requirements because it is the source of both behaviours and it also fixes 'no carry-in', i.e. only a and b feed the outputs. Every non-whitespace character of the 328-character spec is therefore covered. Nothing was invented: the spec states plain one-bit binary inputs and is silent about timing, which the contract pins to zero-latency combinational outputs, so no guessed behaviour was added and there is nothing underdetermined.",
